counterevidence: The feasible 20-epoch SimNPO arm is counterevidence to a blanket claim that more epochs cannot help; the supported claim is method- and regime-specific.
Scope12 helps SimNPO while scope changes did not explain CEU Stage-A endpoints, so wider scope is not a universal prescription.
GradDiff lower ranks materially improve forgetting, so history constraints do affect it; rejection arises from endpoint floors, not absence of rank effect.
findings: CEU history-rank tuning is not feasible under the fixed floors: rank1/2/4 improve ES-Un by only 0.022617/0.012028/0.009119 and all violate retain, utility, and privacy floors; production rank8 remains the bounded fallback.
GradDiff rank1/2 achieve the ES-Un threshold with improvements 0.075057/0.054843, but violate ES-Re and MU floors; the rank frontier does not enter the preregistered feasible region.

SimNPO is proposal-limited under alpha=1: scope6 and scope12 are feasible with zero mean correction at displayed precision; scope12 is selected with ES-Un improvement 0.178046, ES-Re loss 0.006768, MU loss 0.002030, and privacy improvement.
SimNPO gamma0.5/1.0 improve ES-Un by 0.291646/0.509761 but fail the ES-Re floor; gamma should be treated as a retain-boundary control rather than maximized.
SimNPO alpha0 at gamma0.5 collapses ES-Re and MU despite mean correction 0.933807, so first-order GU constraints do not make the explicit retain objective universally redundant.
Twenty epochs is a feasible method-specific diagnostic for SimNPO but cannot be promoted as a universal epoch rule.

Do not launch the four generated Stage-B2 jobs unchanged: one duplicates completed scope12 and the others are not grounded by feasible rank/gamma selectors. Prioritize matched scope3-versus-scope12 seed1/2 replication.
